ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a stack of a total of 54 playing cards is laid flat on a horizontal tabletop, and the mass of each card is m. Press the 1st card with a finger with a vertically downward force, and move the finger to the right at a certain speed, ensuring that there is relative sliding between the finger and the 1st card. Suppose the maximum static friction force is the same as the sliding friction force, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the finger and the 1st card is $\mu_{1}$, the coefficients of kinetic friction between cards are all $\mu_{2}$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the 54th card and the tabletop is $\mu_{3}$, and $\mu_1>\mu_2>\mu_3$. Then which of the following statements is correct? ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Relative sliding cannot occur between the 2nd card and the 53rd card.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a stack of playing cards placed horizontally on a tabletop; the left side marks the topmost as the 1st card and the bottommost as the 54th card; a finger presses on the topmost 1st card, an arrow indicates that the finger moves to the right, and below the stack of cards is a horizontal tabletop. Reasoning: Let the vertical pressure exerted by the finger on the 1st card be F. The normal force between the 1st card and the 2nd card is F+mg, so the maximum friction force that this interface can provide is μ2(F+mg). Regardless of whether the 1st card slides relative to the 2nd card, the horizontal force transmitted by the outside world through the 1st card to the 2nd card and the stack below cannot exceed μ2(F+mg). Now look at any internal adjacent interface between the 2nd card and the 53rd card, let it be between the kth card and the (k+1)th card, where k≥2. This interface bears the finger pressure above it and the weight of the k cards above it, so the normal force is F+kmg, and the friction limit is μ2(F+kmg). Since k≥2, F+kmg>F+mg, therefore μ2(F+kmg)>μ2(F+mg). And the horizontal driving force that these internal interfaces need to transmit can at most only come from the force transmitted in through the interface between the 1st card and the 2nd card, whose upper limit is μ2(F+mg), which is smaller than the friction limit μ2(F+kmg) of the internal interface itself. Therefore the internal interfaces cannot reach the condition for relative sliding. Conclusion: Relative sliding cannot occur between the 2nd card and the 53rd card.
